hypotheses.justification: The theorem also takes `[IsCurveOver K F]`, and `class IsCurveOver : Prop extends HasPrincipalDivisors K F` (Definitions/Def_AlgebraicCurve_IsCurveOver.lean) makes `IsCurveOver.toHasPrincipalDivisors` an instance. Both classes are Props, so the instances are defeq by proof irrelevance. Nothing in the statement (`T.RegularOutside A`, `LSpace 0`, `StichtenothGenusExists K F`) needs HasPrincipalDivisors to elaborate. The same proof `stichtenothGenusExists_of_hasPoleDivisorPackage (hasPoleDivisorPackage_of_isFractionRing T hA)` goes through with the instance found from IsCurveOver (e.g. after `omit [HasPrincipalDivisors K F] in`). This can be deleted together with `[Nonempty (Place K F)]`.

It follows from the other hypotheses. `hasPoleDivisorPackage_of_isFractionRing T hA` (which does not need Nonempty) gives `⟨P⟩ : HasPoleDivisorPackage K F = Nonempty (PoleDivisorPackage K F)`. P has fields `hn_pos : 0 < P.n` and `degB_eq : Divisor.degree P.B = P.n`. If `Place K F` were empty, `Divisor K F = Place K F →₀ ℤ` would be a subsingleton, so `P.B = 0`, and `Divisor.degree 0 = 0` (degree is an AddMonoidHom, `map_zero`), contradicting `0 < n`. So the new proof first obtains P, uses this short argument (`haveI : Nonempty (Place K F) := by by_contra h; rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h; ...`) to get the instance, and then applies `stichtenothGenusExists_of_hasPoleDivisorPackage ⟨P⟩` as before.
